angle: WR/TE Break G (speed shed into the plant and drive out, first cut of Combine route drills) graded by the same code on matched NFL route families; tested against full-season separation over expected on held-out draft classes; why it fails (entry speed tested directly, not all of the gap); drill protocol and coaching line; 2025 day-3 receivers as a coin-flip film aid.
metric_name: Break G: yd/s of velocity a receiver sheds into his plant and redirects out of it over the second around his first cut (1 sd = 0.22 yd/s); compared within drill and Combine year, averaged over route drills, shrunk by each receiver's reliability.
headline_number: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of true Break G [90%: -3.8, 1.0], n=116 receivers, held-out draft classes; flat-prior P(|effect|<3 in) = 90% (3-cone 67%, shuttle 80%). Baseline held-out error 8.6 in route-weighted per receiver, 14.9 in unweighted. Transfer: 40 -> NFL top speed 0.48 vs Combine -> NFL Break G -0.04 (n=92); NFL breaks entered at drill speed 0.04 [-0.05, 0.13], entry speed removed -0.03.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_21/cand_2 applying the four judges' feedback. Data science: held-out error reconciled (route-weighted per receiver 8.6 in as quoted; unweighted 14.9 in, matching the judge's refit) and both now checked by verify.py; flat-prior posterior P(|slope|<3 in) added for Break G, 3-cone and shuttle (Table 1 column); day-3 test moved to the receiver level (28 receivers, one pair each, LOCO forecasts): pick + SOE 39% correct calls vs pick only 54%, -14 points [-32, 0], and demoted to one bottom-line sentence. Football: entry-speed explanation tested directly (NFL breaks entered at drill speed move transfer -0.07 -> 0.04; entry speed removed on both sides -0.03; both far below the 0.22 a true 0.5 would show), stated honestly as part, not all, of the gap; sampling-bias sensitivity (random half +0.13 [-0.05, 0.30] vs top-EPA half -0.19); decision-ready Table 4 of 2025 day-3 receivers with drill Break G, drill->NFL speed shed, flip point and man/zone, slot/wide cell n, labelled a coin-flip film aid; position-coach sentence. Writeup: coach-repeatable definition with yd/s unit, why WR/TE and why now with the 9% pick price as the stake; jargon (hierarchical, inclusion-weighted, class-stratified) removed from body and captions; multiplicity, weights, reliability numbers moved to appendix tables; 3-cone and shuttle as Table 1 rows; receiver table cut to three speeds + takeaway. Viz: Fig 1 rebuilt as three player cards (Boutte, Flournoy, Bobo) with <=5 reps + median, part-by-part bar strip, 10.5pt+ fonts, no clipped titles; Fig 3 = A/B hero pair only with 4 named receivers, ceiling 0.43 and 0.22 both stated in panel and caption; subset panel moved to appendix figB (with the entry-speed tests); Fig 2 x-axis [-8, 6], numbers in a separate column, one legend row, n on subset rows, 'inches of separation' scale in the axis label; figA shows both reliability definitions (0.53 rep-level, 0.50 drill-level). verify.py: 124 of 124 numbers reproduce (68 exact). 1,623 words, 3 figures + 4 tables.
open_risks: Still a null-result paper; the re-stem-at-NFL-speed prescription cannot be tested here, and the entry-speed test shows speed matching explains only part of the gap.

The random-play half gives +0.13 [-0.05, 0.30] while the top-EPA half gives -0.19 [-0.34, -0.03]: the sampled NFL tracking may hide a small transfer; only the season tests (full-season NGS) are free of this.
Power is 68% at the 3-inch margin (80% only at 3.5 in) and harm is not excluded (lower bound -3.8); the flat-prior ROPE probability (90%) depends on the normal approximation to the bootstrap.
Table 4 puts names in the body as a film aid while the receiver-level day-3 test (n=28) cannot order them; the football judge may want more, the data-science judge may want less.
Speed-shed columns in Tables 3 and 4 are differences of medians from few reps (7-9 drill reps per receiver).
